findings.finding: The 2026-08-31 underwriting agreement bars the company (and officers and directors) from selling stock for 90 days after pricing. No ATM draw or shelf takedown can print between today's close and tomorrow's. That removes the commonest second leg down for a sub-$2 biotech.
findings.mechanism_in_window: The lock-up binds every session to about 2026-11-29, including 2026-10-08. The issuer-supply channel is therefore shut for the whole window, unless TD Securities grants a discretionary release, which would itself need an 8-K.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None on this line. The baseline's 12 recent comparable falls show no issuer-supply event inside a next-session window.
findings.why_not_priced: Small by construction. The prospectus is public, so this mostly says what will not happen. A price that held an ATM risk would show heavy volume on the fall; today ran at 0.74x. Offering buyers at $1.21 still hold about a 24% gain and are not locked up, so holder supply remains open. That is why this is sized under one point.
findings.independence: The 2026-09-02 8-K says the proceeds fund operations into Q1 2028, so the company has no near-term cash need: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1699382/000119312526378838/d113784d8k.htm
